A1.justification: Both PDFs describe v-HUB despite the revised title and presentation. All 30 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including appendices, tables, figures and annotation interfaces, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of MLLMs on three benchmark tasks, modality and background-knowledge analyses, and human ratings of generated explanations.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on the expanded benchmark, including AutoDQ scores, annotation-agreement results and qualitative model-response cases.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction procedure, three tasks and model input procedures remain substantively unchanged. Background-knowledge annotation already appears in v1's annotation manual and experiments. AutoDQ changes evaluation, while the additional background-knowledge prompt documents an existing experiment.

E1.justification: v2 incorporates YouTube videos attributed to Xie et al. (2024), broadening the user-generated source pool beyond the existing X and Chaplin sources. The short-video humor domain, three tasks and evaluated input modalities remain the same.

E2.justification: The same seven MLLMs, model sizes and corresponding comparator memberships are retained, including the Qwen2.5-72B and Qwen2.5-7B base-LLM comparisons. Additional datasets in Table 1 are related-work comparisons, not newly evaluated model baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds event-entailment-based AutoDQ evaluation for humor explanations, while retaining BERTScore results in the appendix. Evaluation size increases from 960 to 1218 videos, and the background-knowledge subset grows from 357 to 374. The background-dependent subset comparison is explicitly described as Video-Only in v2, versus Video+Audio in v1's appendix; this establishes a reported setting revision, not proof of rerunning.

E4.justification: v2 adds regional-background profiling in Figure 4d and three case studies comparing caption-matching and QA responses across input modalities in Figure 9. Existing modality, background-knowledge, video-era and base-LLM analyses are retained; their relocation does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: Section 2.4 newly reports annotation consensus using Krippendorff's alpha and categorical agreement levels, with over 90% rated High and 0.3% Low. Category thresholds are unspecified. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty for model scores; the human evaluation remains 50 explanations rated by one annotator.

E6.justification: Aggregate and subgroup scores are extensively revised, and AutoDQ results and qualitative cases are added. For example, Table 2 changes Qwen2.5-VL caption accuracy from 0.719 to 0.726 for text and from 0.673 to 0.666 for video. These are results on an expanded corpus, not controlled performance gains or losses. Table 9's human ratings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theoretical results, proofs or formal derivations. The added AutoDQ description explains an adopted evaluation metric and its standard precision, recall and F1 interpretation, without introducing new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: v2 narrows the novelty rationale by acknowledging prior MLLM humor evaluation instead of describing it as missing. It also removes v1's abstract claim that all models lose caption-matching performance with video input. The principal benchmark contribution and claims about visual difficulty and audio's usefulness remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning English-only annotations and geographical regions as imperfect proxies for culture. Section 4.3 reframes visual text as a complementary cue, acknowledges a Video-SALMONN-2 exception, and softens v1's interpretation that visual text effectively compensates for uninformative sound.

D1.justification: v2 supplies metric-package versions and a background-knowledge caption-matching prompt in Table 27. Appendix A.3 adds explicit reuse restrictions and removal-on-request terms, while v1's promises of broad dataset availability and public code release are not retained. These are documentation and stated-access changes; actual resource availability is not established.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises its central positioning by identifying HumorQA, attributed to Xie et al. (2024), as the closest prior benchmark and contrasting its surprise-focused coverage, duration and treatment of environmental sound. Table 1 adds HumorQA and Oogiri-GO and compares sources, durations and modalities. This replaces v1's broader assertion that parallel video-LLM evaluation was missing.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: data statistics, additional related work and the base-LLM analysis move into the main text; LLM-use disclosures move into acknowledgements; and appendices are regrouped. The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion and ethics text are revised, with a new limitations section and changed title and author listing.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout and extensively restructures tables. v1's Figure 1 is split between v2's Figures 1 and 5; appendix statistics are redesigned and consolidated into main-text Figure 4; and Figure 9 adds case studies. Annotation-interface images are retained, while result tables reorganize metric columns and main-versus-appendix presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves positioning and interpretability through a clearer comparison with the closest prior benchmark, event-coverage evaluation, agreement reporting and specific cultural and language limitations. These gains are constrained by incomplete implementation details and inconsistent new results: Tables 2 and 12 give MiniCPM2.6-o Video+Audio AutoDQ as 0.120 and 0.110, respectively, reversing its small audio effect relative to 0.112 without audio. The revision is more informative, but does not establish substantially stronger experimental reliability.
